title: Managers, and deleting a person
changes: The Admin role is now called Manager everywhere: the top bar, the Manager page, staff list, role choices and messages. Super admins keep their name and still get the Server page.

Delete account: managers and super admins can delete a person from Staff & logins → Edit. They're signed out everywhere and can't sign in again, their email can be used for a new account, and their name stays on past rides and reports. Rides they hadn't started go back in line.
Nobody can delete their own account, and only a super admin can delete a super admin.

title: Ready for other businesses: a blank slate with a Setup page
changes: A brand-new install now starts blank (no business name, address or location built in) and opens on a Setup page: make the first admin account, then enter the business (dealership or shuttle service, name, phone, where the shuttle starts, time zone and colors).
Setup is protected by a one-time setup code shown only on the computer running the site, so nobody who finds the address first can take it over.
Existing sites aren't touched: your name, address, settings, staff and rides stay exactly as they are, and you never see the Setup page.
Cities in reports work anywhere in the US, not just around Boulder.
The README is now a guide for anyone installing or offering the software, and the sample data (npm run seed:demo) is placed around your own location.

title: Remove all staff except super admins
changes: New in Admin → Server: Remove all staff. It shows exactly who will be removed and who's kept, asks you to type REMOVE STAFF, and makes a backup first.
Removed people are signed out everywhere, can't sign in again, and disappear from every list. Their emails can be used for new accounts. Account requests waiting for approval are deleted.
History is kept: past rides, shifts, GPS miles and reports keep everyone's names. Rides a removed driver hadn't started go back in line for the drivers who are left.

title: Cloudflare connection: no more fighting copies
changes: Only one copy of the shuttle program runs at a time. Starting it again (for example the Startup folder plus a double-click) now just says it's already running and closes, instead of starting a second website and a second Cloudflare connection that fight over the same port.
If Shuttle Control was closed without stopping the Cloudflare connection (the window's X, or Task Manager), that leftover connection is stopped before a new one starts.
If Cloudflare's status port is taken anyway, the next try uses another port instead of failing over and over.
Shuttle Control shows why it can't connect (for example “status port in use”, “token refused”, or “can't reach Cloudflare”), and its status now shows its own connection, not a stuck leftover one.

title: Finished rides show when they really happened
changes: The customer's tracking page used to keep showing the scheduled time after the ride, like “Leaving 6:45 PM” on a drop off that already happened (a drop off's scheduled time includes the 30-minute wait). Once the customer is in the shuttle it now shows the real times: “Left the dealership 6:21 PM · Dropped off 6:38 PM”, or “Picked up … · At the dealership …”.
Finished rides no longer say “Look for” the van.

title: Your own name, pictures and web address everywhere
changes: Admin → Settings → Your business: pick Car dealership or Shuttle service (hotel, airport parking, office…), and what riders call your home base. Drivers and customers then see your word everywhere: “bring you to the hotel”, “Back at the hotel”, route stops, texts and emails.

Your branding: besides your name, colors and logo, you can now upload an app icon (the browser tab, phones' home screens and notifications) and a banner photo shown behind your name on the sign-in and customer pages.
Every browser tab shows your name, like “Driver App · Your Business”, and “Add to Home Screen” uses your name, colors and icon.
Web address: type your own address (like shuttle.yourbusiness.com) in Settings, tap Check to make sure it reaches this shuttle PC, and every link, text, email and QR code uses it.
Optional short link for customers, like yourbusiness.com/ride, that opens the ride request page. QR codes use it.
The “Corwin” look is now called the Branded look.
Fix: “Today” and “Booked ahead” lists now split at midnight in the business's time zone, whatever the shuttle PC's clock is set to.

title: Phone & email your way, detailed reports, and a daily report at midnight
changes: New Admin → Phone & email tab. Each dealership chooses how calls and texts work: staff use their own phones, or a dealership number so customers only ever see the dealership.

With a dealership number, tapping Call rings the staff member's phone and connects them to the customer; tapping Text sends from the dealership number and keeps the message on the ride. You also pick which number customers see, and who a call to the shuttle number rings: the driver on that customer's ride, every driver on shift, or a desk phone. Texts to the number are added to the customer's ride.
The dealership number (Twilio) is set up right on that tab, with a test call and the links to paste into Twilio. The auth token stays on the shuttle PC.

Email uses the dealership's own email system and a shared mailbox. The site won't accept a staff member's own email address. Choose the name emails come from, where replies go, and which emails are sent (password links, “your account is ready”, and new: “your ride is booked” to customers who give an email).

Reports: drivers now show shifts, time on shift, people carried, rides per hour, drive time to the pick up, wait at the pick up, no-shows and GPS gaps. New Vehicles table (shifts, time in use, GPS miles), Busiest hours, and a Ride log with every ride's times you can download.
No-shows marked by drivers (“Customer didn't come out”) are now counted in reports.

New daily report (Admin → Server → Daily reports): the shuttle's day plus how the server did: requests, server errors, response times, the slowest requests, page speed on real devices, and the most common errors in the log. It can be emailed to managers each morning.
At midnight, in this order: the day's report is saved, customer info is cleared, then the nightly backup runs, so everything is backed up at midnight (it used to be 12:30 AM).

title: Ride-app touches: who's coming, “I'm here”, and the wait right now
changes: Customers see who's coming: the driver's first name and photo, the van's color and model, and the plate in big letters.
The tracking page says how many stops the driver makes first (“Sam has 2 stops before you”), or “You're next!”.
Drivers add their photo on the driver page (an admin can add or remove it too, under Edit).

New “📍 I'm here” button for drivers at the pick-up spot. The customer gets a text (if texting is on), and their page shows “Your shuttle is here” with a countdown and two buttons: “I'm coming out” and “I need 5 more minutes”. The driver and advisor see the answer right away.
After the wait (5 minutes, set in Admin → Settings), the driver can cancel the ride as a no-show. Tapped “I'm here” too early? “Not here yet” undoes it.

Shuttle wait right now: the advisor desk and BDC page show how long a pick up booked now would take (“Shuttle is busy: about 25 min · 2 of 3 vans out”), and the customer request page says “We can get to you in about 15 min”.

title: People can have more than one role
changes: In Admin → Staff & logins, tick every role a person has: Service advisor, BDC, Shuttle driver and Admin. For example, an advisor who also drives the shuttle, or a BDC person who drives.
They can use every page for their roles, with a link to each in the top bar. Pick which page they open to when they sign in.
Someone who also drives can start a shift, shows up in the driver lists, gets ride offers and can be assigned rides, and keeps their advisor or BDC desk.
Approving an account request lets you tick several roles too. The staff list shows them all, like “Advisor + Driver”.

title: Updates show up with one reload, or none
changes: After an update, screens switch to the new version by themselves: right away when a page is just opened, not on screen, or nobody has used it for 2 minutes. No more reloading several times.
Pages left open all day (advisor desk, driver phones) find out about an update the moment the site comes back after updating.
If someone is in the middle of something (a window open, typing, a half-filled ride form), the page waits and shows “A newer version is ready” instead. One tap on Reload gets the new version.

title: The BDC desk
changes: New BDC page for the BDC team. Find a customer by name, phone number (any format) or RO number while they're on the phone, and see what to tell them: “Driver on the way · driver Sam in Shuttle 2” or “#2 in line”.
Book a ride with the same step-by-step form as the advisor desk, for today or a future appointment, then send the tracking link right away.
Today, Booked ahead and Finished (last 3 days) lists, plus a live map of the vans. No driver controls.

BDC picks the customer's service advisor when booking (required), and can change it under Edit. The advisor gets a phone notification and a note at the top of the advisor desk (“📞 Bea (BDC) booked a pick up for you”), and the ride is under My customers only.
Rides show who booked them: “Advisor: Kim · 📞 booked by Bea (BDC)”.
Pick BDC as the role when adding someone, approving an account request, or editing a person. BDC staff land on their page when they sign in, and can still open the advisor desk.

title: Spectator links: watch a driver live
changes: Admin → QR codes & links → Spectator links: make a link anyone can open to watch one driver, or every driver on shift, live on a map, without signing in.
The map shows the van moving, speed, battery, when it last updated, and the planned route line. No customer names, phone numbers or addresses.
Links work for 1, 4, 12 or 24 hours, and you can revoke one any time. The list shows how many times each was opened.

title: Driver location always on, with a low-battery setting
changes: The driver page shares the phone's location whenever it's open, on shift or not. Drivers can't switch it off themselves unless an admin allows it.

New in Admin → Settings → Driver location: when a phone's battery is low (you pick the level, 20% by default) and it isn't charging, share less often (about every 30 seconds), pause until it's plugged in, or keep sharing as normal. Android phones only; iPhones don't tell websites their battery level.
A bar at the top of the driver page always shows what's happening, for example “🔋 Battery 15%: sharing less often to save battery. Plug in to go back to normal.”
Admins and advisors see each driver's phone battery on the van map (🔋 15%, or charging).
During a shift the screen stays on so the phone keeps sharing, except on a low battery.

title: New staff can ask for an account
changes: New staff tap “Ask for an account” on the sign-in page. They enter their name, work email, phone, Advisor or Driver, and a password they choose.
Admins get a phone notification. The request shows at the top of Staff & logins with Approve (pick the role) or Decline.
Until it's approved, signing in says it's waiting for an admin. Once approved, they sign in with the password they chose, and get an email if email is set up.
Nobody can ask to be an admin. Admins can turn the link off in Settings.

title: Rotation near the dealership, right destinations, full check-up
changes: Rotation: a driver coming back to the dealership with customers on board (next stop the dealership, or within 3 miles of it) is offered a ride waiting within 3 miles of them. Drop off, then grab the next one. Taking it updates their route automatically.
A trip that passes the dealership with picked-up customers on board stops to let them off before going on.
Navigate on a ride goes where the driver needs to go next: the dealership when a picked-up customer is on board or a drop-off customer is still waiting there.
Re-planning a route always includes customers already in the van, so they're never forgotten.
Browsers that visit over https always come back over https.
Full check-up after this week's updates: 68 automated tests, every page in every role and look, races, 1,933 odd requests, live site through Cloudflare, and a 1,000-person load test.

title: Smarter routes: dealership stops along the way, urgent rides first
changes: Routes can now stop at the dealership in the middle of a trip: drop off the customers picked up so far, collect drop-off customers who are ready, then head out again. No more riding everyone around until the end.
Urgent rides and rides due soonest come first. Being late counts far more than a few extra minutes of driving, and urgent rides count three times as much again.
Routes avoid showing up long before a customer is due: the driver arrives about 10 minutes early instead.
Seats are respected the whole way. A trip with more people than seats goes back to the dealership in between instead of being refused.
Each dealership stop says who gets off and who gets on, and pick ups that will be late are marked.
A pick-up stop leaves the route as soon as the customer is on board.

title: Password resets in seconds
changes: “Forgot password?” now sends the reset link straight to the person by email in seconds, instead of waiting for an admin. Set up the email account in Admin → Settings → Email for password resets (Microsoft 365, Gmail, or any provider), and use “Send a test to me” to check it.
If texting is set up, people with a phone number on file get the link by text too.
The link works once, for 1 hour. If nothing can be sent, admins are alerted like before.
The email password stays on the shuttle PC and is never shown or sent to browsers.

title: Routes start where the van is, and links always use https
changes: Driver routes no longer start from an old location. If the phone hasn't shared where it is in the last 10 minutes, the route starts at the dealership instead of where the van was hours ago.
Maps show only the part of a route still ahead (from the van onward), on the driver's map and on the admin and advisor maps.
QR codes and customer links now always start with https:// for people using the site through its web address.

title: Short customer links and a handier customer page
changes: Tracking links are short and easy to read, like corwinshuttleservice.com/t/K7M2Q9XA, with no look-alike letters, and any case works. Links sent before still work.
Customer QR codes are simpler (fewer, bigger squares), so they scan faster even when printed small.
The customer page shows a big countdown (“Arriving in about 8 min”), even when the driver isn't on a planned route.
Big one-tap buttons for customers: Call, Text us, Add to calendar, and Share (for family picking them up).
Customers can say they're running late (5, 10, 15 or 20+ min) or cancel with a reason. The driver and advisor get a notification and it shows on the ride. Admins can turn this off in Settings.
Wrong tracking codes are limited, so nobody can guess other customers' links.

title: Opens instantly, and page speed from real devices
changes: Phones and computers keep the site's screens and map images, so the shuttle site opens instantly after the first visit, even on slow Wi-Fi or a slow network. Rides and tracking always come fresh from the server; no customer details are kept on devices.
After an update, the screen still opens instantly and a bar offers the newer version with a Reload button.
If the server is slow to answer, a “Still connecting…” note shows instead of a frozen screen.

New on Admin → Server: Page speed on real devices. It shows how long each part of loading takes on staff and customer devices (finding the address, connecting, waiting for the shuttle PC, downloading, building the page, rides, and map images) and lists slow loads with what held them up.
After an update, phones only download the files that changed.
Maps use one map server address instead of three, and connect to it right away. The main fonts start loading straight away.
Driver page: no stray “· ·” when a van has no make or model.

title: No more double wins
changes: If two drivers tap the same ride at the same moment, only one gets it. The other is told it's taken. (With the site on several cores, both could be told they had it.)
Two drivers can't start a shift in the same van at the same moment, and the ride back is booked only once even if two people tap "Customer ready" together.
Adding two staff with the same email at once gives a clear message.
Odd or broken requests get a clear answer instead of "Something went wrong".

title: Bug fixes from a full sweep
changes: Editing a ride that's already urgent now keeps the “Why is it urgent?” box required.
Closing a pop-up window with Escape, the backdrop or its own buttons now always cleans up and puts the keyboard back where you were.
Full check of every page, for every role, on phone and computer, light and dark, in both looks, with the site on 4 cores: no other problems found.

title: Tidier shutdowns
changes: When the site stops or restarts, its copies on each core stop quietly instead of filling the log with harmless errors.

title: Uses every processor core; memory and bandwidth limits; traffic by kind
changes: The site now runs one copy of itself per processor core, so it stays fast when lots of people use it at once.
Super admins choose the number of cores, a memory limit and a bandwidth limit in Admin → Server → Cores, memory & bandwidth.
If the site goes over the memory limit, the copy using the most memory restarts by itself, and screens reconnect in seconds.
Traffic chart: see each kind of traffic (pages, files, ride lists, van maps, driver GPS, customer tracking, sign-ins, admin) and turn each on or off. Switch between requests and data sent.
Sign-in and request limits are counted across every copy of the site.

title: Corwin look for everyone, faster and steadier
changes: The Corwin look is now the site's look for everyone (you can switch back in Settings → Look).
Version numbers: admins see the version in the top bar and what changed in each update.
Much faster with many people on the site: ride lists, van maps and tracking pages are built once and shared.
Screens catch up by themselves after the connection drops or the site restarts.
Moving vans no longer make every screen reload the ride lists; less traffic over Cloudflare.
Driver phones check for offers less often (offers still pop up instantly).
Escape closes pop-up windows.

title: Vehicles: fuel, shuttle or loaner, and the fleet list
changes: Each vehicle has a fuel type (gas, hybrid, plug-in, electric) and is a Shuttle or a Loaner.
Drivers can only start a shift in a shuttle.
Import the dealership's vehicle list (.xlsx or .csv) with a preview; active vehicles stay active.

title: Staff privacy, super admins, QR page, Discord help
changes: Staff list shows names only; email, phone and access are under Edit.
The Server page is for super admins only.
Links and QR codes use https; new QR page with a printable sign.
💬 Help button for help requests and ideas, sent to Discord.

title: Instant updates and Cloudflare tools
changes: Changes show up on every screen right away.
Shuttle Control shows the Cloudflare connection and can run it.
Speed test in Admin → Server.

title: Server tools, reports, step-by-step booking
changes: Admin → Server: health, live numbers, log, backups and restart; Shuttle Control window on the server PC.
Reports: miles, time driving, cities, advisor scheduling.
Booking in five short steps; drop offs wait 30 minutes unless urgent (with a reason).
Corwin look (preview), and Taco Tuesday. 🌮

title: The shuttle website
changes: Advisor, driver and admin pages with maps, pick up / drop off and what to do first.
Customer request and tracking pages, QR codes and links.
Sign-ins with password reset, phone notifications, route planner, ride offers and the seat limit.
Automatic updates, nightly sign-out and customer-info clearing.
